title: Repeated decrement execution
statement: Let $A$ be a register program with $m$ registers and $d$ oracle queries, let $\Lambda$ be its set of labels, and fix an input $y$, a register $r$, labels $\ell_i$ for $i\in\mathbb N$, and natural numbers $k,B$. Suppose that for every $i<k$, label $\ell_i$ instructs the program to decrement register $r$ and continue at $\ell_{i+1}$; initially every register is at most $B$ and the value in register $r$ is at least $k$. Then the program has a finite execution from label $\ell_0$ to label $\ell_k$, with register $r$ reduced by $k$ and all other register values unchanged. Every configuration before the endpoint satisfies the program's guard: its instruction is safe to execute and every register remains at most $B$.
hypotheses_covered: A program A with m registers and d oracle queries
A label sequence indexed by natural numbers
Each of the first k labels decrements r and continues at the next label
Every initial register value is at most B
The initial value of r is at least k
